A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) antihypertensives are effective in reducing blood pressure (BP); (2) the magnitude of BP decrease varies according to the antihypetensive used; (3) sex, ethnicity, and body mass index are associated with antireperensives response; and (4) the combination of antihypetensives can lead to greater reductions in blood pressure than monotherapy.
, in the case of monotherapy, all drugs have a similar BP-lowering efficacy, whereas in the case of combination therapy, olmesartans, valsartan, and felodipine-based drugs are more effective.
